premises.statement: The required channel efficiency formula applies additional factors of 0.3 and 0.4 to the CTR and ROAS deltas before applying their respective blend weights.
premises.alternative: The contract specifies a "weighted blend of CTR delta (30%), ROAS delta (40%), and avg_campaign_health_score (30%)" without specifying these additional inner multipliers.
premises.reason: The additional scaling changes scores and the growth-opportunity flags derived from them.

premises.statement: Channel strategic recommendations require only the implemented ROI, underperforming-share, and momentum rules.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: CASE WHEN roas<.5 AND total_spend>1000 THEN 'Review ROI and reduce inefficient spend' WHEN underperforming_pct>50 ... WHEN high_momentum_pct>50 ...
premises.alternative: The column description specifies priority rules using "ROAS vs channel benchmark, spend share, top-tier share, underperforming share, momentum, and health score"; several of these inputs are unused.
premises.reason: Omitted decision inputs and unestablished thresholds can change recommendations across the report.

premises.statement: Every retained channel group includes at least one campaign classified as Premium Investment.
premises.alternative: The contract describes "premium_spend for investment_tier = Premium Investment" and its percentage of total spend; a group without such campaigns could require zero rather than the NULL returned by an empty filtered sum.
premises.reason: Groups without premium campaigns receive missing investment amounts and percentages instead of numeric zero.

premises.statement: Averaging four-decimal rounded CPA values is an acceptable implementation of the unrounded device CPA benchmark.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: round(CASE WHEN total_conversions>0 THEN total_spend/total_conversions END,4) cost_per_conversion; avg(cost_per_conversion) over(partition by device,date_day)
premises.alternative: The contract says device_benchmark_cpa is "not rounded" and is the average CPA using rows with conversions.
premises.reason: Premature rounding changes benchmarks and their percentage deltas.

premises.statement: Conversion-value sums are nonnegative for every retained channel group.
premises.alternative: The output description requires a "non-negative monetary amount", but the upstream campaign model's final filter checks conversions rather than conversions_value.
premises.reason: No implemented validation establishes the required sign of this output.

premises.statement: The implemented acquisition recommendation rules are complete without considering days since first conversion or active campaign count.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: CASE WHEN ltv_cac_ratio>=3 AND cac_efficiency_percentile>=.8 ... WHEN channel_diversity_count<2 ... WHEN cac_vs_cohort_pct>30 ...
premises.alternative: The contract requires ordered rules using "ltv_cac_ratio, cac_efficiency_percentile, channel_diversity_count, days_since_first_conversion, CAC vs cohort, and active_campaigns_count".
premises.reason: Two explicitly named decision inputs are omitted and the chosen thresholds are not established.

premises.statement: Acquisition sophistication awards one LTV point per 100 currency units and five points per unit of LTV:CAC before applying the specified caps.
premises.alternative: The contract specifies only "up to 30 from average_customer_ltv, and up to 25 from ltv_cac_ratio", without giving these scaling factors.
premises.reason: The selected scales determine how quickly customers reach high sophistication scores.

premises.statement: Averages of rounded row-level CAC and LTV values satisfy the required unrounded cohort benchmarks.
premises.alternative: The contract requires averaging "cumulative_acquisition_cost / cumulative_conversions" and "cumulative_ltv / cumulative_conversions", with benchmarks "not rounded".
premises.reason: Using already-rounded economics changes cohort comparisons and potentially recommendations.

premises.statement: Computing LTV:CAC from unrounded cumulative ratios is equivalent to dividing the rounded average_customer_ltv by the rounded customer_acquisition_cost.
premises.alternative: The business logic defines ltv_cac_ratio as "average_customer_ltv divided by customer_acquisition_cost", after specifying two-decimal rounding for both inputs.
premises.reason: Different rounding order can change ratio thresholds used in segmentation and alerts.

premises.statement: Every retained acquisition row has positive cumulative conversions and a non-null cohort CAC benchmark.
premises.alternative: The contract permits spend-only accounts with no first conversion, while requiring these alerts to be non-null and "else false".
premises.reason: Spend-only accounts can produce NULL alerts because the comparisons are not given false fallbacks.

premises.statement: Each account's executive-dashboard observations are consecutive daily rows, so a seven-row lag identifies the value seven calendar days earlier.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: lag(total_spend,7) over(partition by account_id order by date_day); lag(total_conversions,7) over(partition by account_id order by date_day)
premises.alternative: The executive contract specifies comparison with the "value 7 days prior", which differs from seven preceding observations when dates are missing or repeated.
premises.reason: This extends the earlier unverified row-offset assumption to executive weekly growth calculations.

premises.statement: Every retained executive row has either two non-null weekly growth percentages or at least one weekly growth condition that evaluates to true.
premises.alternative: The contract allows missing prior values to produce NULL growth percentages but requires trending_alert to be "else false" and non-null.
premises.reason: Early observations and missing lag baselines can otherwise produce NULL alert values.

premises.statement: Every retained executive account-date has at least one globally observed keyword.
premises.alternative: The contract explicitly replaces missing keyword counts with zero and requires scale_opportunity to be "else false" and non-null.
premises.reason: Dates without keywords produce a NULL percentage and therefore a NULL flag.

premises.statement: The executive rolling averages already have the required output precision before the additional rounded columns are appended.
premises.alternative: The contract requires final rounding to 2, 4, and 1 decimal places respectively; SELECT * retains the original same-named columns alongside the rounded expressions.
premises.reason: The final name-based selection depends on retaining the intended rounded values rather than the original averages.

premises.statement: Rounding portfolio percentages to two decimals before threshold comparisons does not change any executive recommendation or flag.
premises.alternative: The contract applies thresholds directly to safe-divided count ratios, such as "star_performer_keywords/active_keywords > 0.15", without intermediate rounding.
premises.reason: Ratios slightly above a boundary can round down to it and receive a different classification.
